item.title: Siri Remote for Vibe Coding 1.0.1
item.description:
# Siri Remote for Vibe Coding 1.0.1
The first release of this fork under its new name: use the USB-C Apple TV Siri Remote (3rd generation) as a programmable macOS controller for AI coding.
## Highlights
- **Instant push-to-talk shortcuts:** pressing Siri holds the recorded shortcut immediately; releasing Siri releases that shortcut. You can keep holding it without entering later hold stages. - **Before and after talking:** optionally switch to an open app, tap an **On Press** shortcut, hold the push-to-talk shortcut, and tap an **On Release** shortcut such as Enter. - **Macros:** add and remove keystrokes with **+ / −**, and adjust the delay between them. Switching from a populated macro to another action no longer crashes the editor. - **Optional touch surface:** disable touch movement, scrolling and swipes from Layout. - **Layer and App management:** rename/delete optional layers, manage app profiles, and copy another layer with **Copy From**. New layers are independent; their unassigned inputs do nothing. - **More reliable held modifiers:** moving a physical mouse while holding a remote shortcut preserves Ctrl and other held modifiers, so push-to-talk is not interrupted by mouse movement. - **Reorganized Settings:** Layout → Voice → Tuning; Manage Layers sits beside Manage Apps, and Copy From follows the Editing label. Native Voice functionality remains available. - **New branding throughout:** application, installer/uninstaller, documentation and release assets use Siri Remote for Vibe Coding; compact surfaces use Siri Remote Vibe. - **Updates belong to this fork:** update URLs point to this repository, and 1.0.1 embeds the fork's own Sparkle public key. Future App updates are authenticated with that key.
## Downloads
Requires **macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon**. Windows is not supported by this release.
- **App only:** `SiriRemoteVibe-1.0.1-macOS-arm64.zip`. Quit the old app, back it up, and place `Siri Remote for Vibe Coding.app` in Applications. Choose this if your microphone components are already installed, or you only need button/shortcut control. - **Full Setup:** `SiriRemoteVibe-Full-Setup-1.0.1-arm64.pkg`. Installs the app, optional Siri Remote Mic components, capture service and uninstaller using the native macOS Installer. - **Alternative Full Setup:** `SiriRemoteVibe-Full-Setup-1.0.1-arm64.zip`. Contains a setup app using the same verified payload and installer routine. - **Checksums:** `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers all three downloads.
These app bundles are **ad-hoc signed and not notarized**; the native installer package is unsigned. macOS may require right-click → **Open** / **Open Anyway** and new Accessibility/Input Monitoring approval. Keep Gatekeeper enabled. Only one UI instance should run at a time.
## Upgrade and compatibility
Install **1.0.1 manually once** if you are using HyperVibe, SiriRemoteForge or an earlier local build. Those builds trust the upstream Sparkle key, which cannot verify this fork's releases. After installing 1.0.1, future automatic App updates use this fork's signing key.
Your existing `~/.config/siriremote/config.jsonc`, Voice data and persistent app identifier are preserved. Full Setup migrates the legacy installed app/uninstaller names. When using the App-only archive, quit and move the old `HyperVibe.app` out of Applications yourself before launching the new app.
Push-to-talk shortcuts control the target app's voice feature and its selected microphone. A shortcut alone does not expose the remote's microphone to macOS. For Siri Remote audio, install the optional Siri Remote Mic stack and Apple's **PacketLogger** from Additional Tools for Xcode separately; PacketLogger is not bundled in these public downloads. Sparkle updates only the App; microphone system-component upgrades require Full Setup.
## Verification
The release is checked for engine behavior, packaged Voice self-checks, held-modifier handling, microphone parser/ring behavior, HAL contracts and offline audio handoff. Archive audits verify checksums, code signatures, payload seals, version/build numbers, architecture, updater key/URLs, licenses and absence of personal config, credentials and PacketLogger. The published App archive is also downloaded and verified against the committed Sparkle public key.
